newsitem.title: POLAND: Nomura says Polish Lentex issue price fully valued.
newsitem.headline: Nomura says Polish Lentex issue price fully valued.

text.p: The 21.5-zloty issue price of the current initial public offering of Polish carpet maker Lentex SA fully values the company, Nomura Equity Research said in a report.
Lentex's offering of 1.5 million shares ends Wednesday.

"On pure fundamentals...the shares look fully valued at the issue price, even if current stock market conditions will probably push the shares to a premium when they start to trade," the report dated January 27 said.

Nomura said its 1997 price-earnings ratio of 10.8 for Lentex was at a discount to the 1997 industrial average of 17 "but not as great a one as might have been expected given the earnings outlook and the market risk," the report said.
Nomura saw Lentex's pre-tax profit at 14.8 million zlotys in 1996, 15.6 million zlotys in 1997 and 17.6 million zlotys in 1998 compared to 18.3 million zlotys in 1995.

It said earnings-per-share growth from 2.1 zlotys estimated for 1996, to two zlotys for 1997 and 2.2 zlotys for 1998 would be slow, in part because the firm's stategy to invest heavily in expanding its product range was a long-term one.

Nomura said the virtual zero eps growth over the next two years would also be due to declining demand for pvc flooring products, in which the firm should derive 55 percent of 1996 sales, and for which it is using the issue's proceeds to build a production line.
The report said that though the IPO might prove popular investors might be wiser to wait to buy in the aftermarket.
